cls: Ornithine decarboxylase inhibitor (antiprotozoal / antineoplastic / topical hair-growth inhibitor)
pharm: Irreversibly inhibits ornithine decarboxylase, reducing polyamine synthesis - slowing facial hair growth topically, killing trypanosomes intravenously, and reducing neuroblastoma relapse orally.
quick: Topical 13.9% cream twice daily; IV ~100 mg/kg q6h x14 days for sleeping sickness; oral IWILFIN BSA-based twice daily
Topical/IV: not applicable; oral tablets with or without food
Avoid systemic use unless benefit outweighs risk; topical use only if needed
Systemic use - avoid breastfeeding; topical - use caution
IV eflornithine is renally eliminated - reduce dose in renal impairment
Monitor LFTs with oral use (hepatotoxicity reported)
Topical: skin reactions; IV/oral: CBC, audiogram, LFTs
summary: Eflornithine is an irreversible ornithine decarboxylase (ODC) inhibitor used in three distinct settings. As a topical 13.9% cream (Vaniqa) it slows the growth of unwanted facial hair in women. Intravenously it treats the meningoencephalitic (late) stage of West African (Trypanosoma brucei gambiense) sleeping sickness, classically about 100 mg/kg every 6 hours for 14 days, often combined with nifurtimox. As oral tablets (IWILFIN), it is FDA-approved to reduce the risk of relapse in high-risk neuroblastoma after at least a partial response to prior therapy. Systemic forms can cause myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity, and hearing loss.
indications: Topical: reduction of unwanted facial hair in women (hirsutism)
Intravenous: treatment of the meningoencephalitic (late) stage of Trypanosoma brucei gambiense (West African) sleeping sickness, usually combined with nifurtimox (NECT)

Oral (IWILFIN): to reduce the risk of relapse in adult and pediatric patients with high-risk neuroblastoma who have had at least a partial response to prior multiagent, multimodality therapy including anti-GD2 immunotherapy

dosage.d: Apply a thin layer of 13.9% cream to affected facial areas twice daily, at least 8 hours apart
dosage.n: Do not wash treated area for at least 4 hours; continue other hair-removal as needed

dosage.c: Late-stage T. b. gambiense sleeping sickness (IV)
dosage.d: Approximately 100 mg/kg IV every 6 hours for 14 days (monotherapy); in NECT, IV eflornithine 200 mg/kg every 12 hours for 7 days plus oral nifurtimox for 10 days
Body-surface-area-based dosing (per FDA Table 1) twice daily until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or a maximum of 2 years
dosage.n: Tablets may be swallowed whole, chewed, or crushed and mixed with soft food/liquid; perform baseline audiogram, CBC, and LFTs

admin: Topical: apply thin layer to dry facial skin, rub in; do not wash area for at least 4 hours; effect is reversible if stopped
IV: infuse over about 2 hours in a monitored setting; dilute per protocol
Oral IWILFIN: take twice daily with or without food; tablets may be swallowed whole, chewed, or crushed/mixed
Before starting oral/IV therapy obtain baseline complete blood count, liver function tests, and audiogram
Adjust or interrupt systemic dosing for myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity, or hearing loss
moa: Eflornithine (DFMO) is an irreversible ('suicide') inhibitor of ornithine decarboxylase, the rate-limiting enzyme converting ornithine to putrescine in polyamine biosynthesis. Depleting polyamines (putrescine, spermidine, spermine) impairs cell proliferation. In the skin it slows the rate of hair follicle growth (without removing existing hair). In Trypanosoma brucei gambiense, ODC inhibition is lethal because the parasite cannot replace the enzyme rapidly. In neuroblastoma, ODC blockade reduces the polyamine drive that supports tumor cell proliferation, lowering relapse risk.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to eflornithine or any component (the oral IWILFIN label lists no formal contraindications)
relative: Renal impairment (IV - renal elimination, dose adjustment needed)
monitor: Systemic: liver function tests and audiogram (hearing loss)

preg: Systemic (IV/oral) eflornithine can cause harm in pregnancy based on mechanism; advise effective contraception during oral therapy and avoid unless the benefit clearly outweighs risk. In late-stage sleeping sickness the disease itself is fatal, so treatment is given when needed. Topical use: only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether eflornithine is excreted in human milk in significant amounts. For systemic (IV/oral) therapy, avoid breastfeeding because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the infant. For topical use, exercise caution.
renal: Eflornithine is eliminated primarily by the kidneys. With IV use, reduce the dose in renal impairment and monitor closely. Topical absorption is minimal, so renal dosing is not relevant for the cream.
hepatic: Oral eflornithine (IWILFIN) can cause hepatotoxicity; monitor liver function tests at baseline and during treatment and adjust or interrupt dosing for significant elevations. Topical use does not require hepatic adjustment.

major: Other myelosuppressive chemotherapy (systemic) - additive bone marrow suppression
moderate: Other ototoxic agents (e.g., aminoglycosides, platinum agents) - additive hearing loss with systemic use
Other hepatotoxic drugs - additive liver injury with oral use
minor: No clinically significant interactions for topical use
interactions.food: Oral tablets may be taken with or without food; topical/IV not applicable.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; limit alcohol with oral use given hepatotoxicity risk.
interactions.diagnostics: Systemic use can lower blood counts and raise liver enzymes; obtain baseline audiogram, CBC, and LFTs.

common: Topical: acne, stinging/burning, skin irritation, folliculitis, rash
Systemic: hearing loss, diarrhea, fever, nausea/vomiting, anemia

counsel: Topical cream slows facial hair growth but does not remove hair - keep using your usual hair-removal methods and allow several weeks to see effect; hair returns if you stop
Apply the cream to a thin layer twice a day, at least 8 hours apart, and do not wash the area for 4 hours
For the IV or oral forms, this is a serious medicine - attend all blood tests and hearing checks
Report unusual bruising/bleeding, fever, yellowing of skin/eyes, or changes in hearing
Tell your doctor about all other medicines, especially other chemotherapy or antibiotics
pk: Topical: visible hair-growth reduction after ~4-8 weeks; systemic: rapid enzyme inhibition
Minimal systemic absorption from the cream; IV peaks at end of infusion
Effect is reversible (topical hair regrows; ODC activity recovers as cells replace enzyme)
Store at controlled room temperature; do not freeze the cream
pearls: Same molecule, three very different uses: topical cream for facial hirsutism, IV for late-stage West African sleeping sickness, and oral tablets (IWILFIN) for high-risk neuroblastoma relapse
IV for sleeping sickness is the 'resurrection drug' - dramatically reverses the meningoencephalitic (late) stage; now usually combined with nifurtimox (NECT)
Topical effect is suppressive only - hair returns about 8 weeks after stopping
Systemic toxicity triad: myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity, and hearing loss - monitor CBC, LFTs, and audiogram
Eflornithine is effective against T. b. gambiense (West African) but not T. b. rhodesiense (East African) sleeping sickness
missed: Topical: if you miss an application, apply it when you remember unless it is nearly time for the next dose, then skip it. Oral IWILFIN: take a missed dose when remembered the same day; if close to the next dose, skip it - do not double up. IV doses are given by clinical staff on schedule.
overdose: There is limited overdose experience. Systemic overdose may intensify myelosuppression, gastrointestinal toxicity, hepatotoxicity, hearing loss, and (with IV) seizures. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive with monitoring of blood counts, liver function, and hearing, and treatment of complications. Topical overuse may cause increased local skin irritation.
